comment: Structural relaxations of a water molecule by Fortran PARSEC (development version 1.4.x, gfortran 13.3, 4 MPI processes).  'structures' are read from parsec.out with Output_Level 2: total energy in Ry with eight decimals, coordinates in bohr and forces in Ry/bohr with six, from the table of total forces after the net force was set to zero, which is what domove receives; 'energy_per_atom_ev' and 'maximum_force' are the numbers of the energy line of atom.cor.  'files' are the files PARSEC wrote (or read: manual.dat, relax_restart_in.dat), byte for byte.  'restart_from' names the case whose relax_restart.dat the run started from.  A Python run needs Hartree_Boundary_Tolerance: off to use PARSEC's Hartree boundary values.  Written by a generator script from the files of those Fortran runs.

RUNNING THE L-BFGS-B CODE

nact  = number of active bounds at the generalized Cauchy point
sub   = manner in which the subspace minimization terminated:
        con = converged, bnd = a bound was reached
itls  = number of iterations performed in the line search
stepl = step length used
tstep = norm of the displacement (total step)
projg = norm of the projected gradient
